content.comment_body: I'm using a [product_name] module, and when I insert a standard SIM card, it connects over UMTS and GPRS for data. I haven't had success with LTE connections yet. However, when I try a specialist static IP SIM, the device fails to connect for data—it displays a DNS address of 0.0.0.0 and no IP address is assigned. The SIM is a roaming type that connects to the strongest available network, and I’ve tested this with two separate suppliers. I can confirm the SIM cards work because they connect fully when used in my TP-Link router. Why would the SIM function in the router but not in the [product_name]? Could it be that the module only works with LTE or there’s an issue around 4G compatibility? Any guidance would be appreciated, and I can provide more details if necessary.
Is anyone able to help? [user_name]? Any advice would be very helpful! I’ve been stuck with this for months.
Apologies, I don’t have experience with the [product_name] and unfortunately can’t assist.

I found a solution after discussing with two suppliers of static public IP SIMs (both roaming types), but neither could pinpoint the issue. It appears there’s a conflict between the roaming capabilities of these SIMs and the [product_name]. I obtained a fixed public IP SIM locked to a single provider, and everything works now. I have HTTPS access to the module (although not to the [product_name] web server), and full VPN access to both [product_name] (including the web server) and the module. This situation might only affect UK users or certain roaming SIMs as I’ve only tried two types. Hope this helps others with similar problems. My next task is deploying a website on AWS, so another learning curve begins!

analysis.insight_summary: The user encountered trouble establishing a data connection on the [product_name] when using roaming static IP SIM cards, even though regular SIMs were able to connect using UMTS and GPRS. The device failed to assign DNS and IP addresses to roaming SIMs, though those SIMs worked in a different network device. The issue was resolved by using a fixed public IP SIM card restricted to one network provider, highlighting a compatibility or configuration challenge with certain roaming SIMs and the [product_name]. Direct HTTPS access to the module was possible, while full remote access including web server functionality required VPN connectivity.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects reliable data connectivity on the [product_name] with any type of SIM card, including static IP roaming SIMs, and similar performance to other network devices. They seek dependable remote access via both web interface and VPN.
